comment: The format-neutral interchange concept vocabulary. Concepts are capability
atoms: refusal and loss messages are only as precise as the vocabulary, so
The vocabulary is append-only. Adding a concept is a data change. Removing
one, or changing what one means, is a design change: every committed format
table is written against these ids.
'detect' declares whether the census walker over a timeline Project can
observe the concept. 'model' concepts are read off the document; 'format'
concepts exist only in some interchange format and are never recorded by a
census. A concept whose model representation lands later flips to 'model'
in the same change that teaches the walker to find it.

concepts.summary: A construct the reader could not classify. No format lists it, so it always refuses.
A track holding clips directly, with no children.
A track that contains other tracks (folder/group/nested scope).
A track whose content is picture rather than audio or notes.
A clip anchored to musical time (canonical ticks).
A clip anchored to absolute time (samples at a rational rate).
Clip content that is a set of note events.
Clip content that references a media asset.
Per-clip gain applied to the clip's content.
Per-clip fade in and fade out durations.
An overlap between two adjacent clips authored as one transition item.
A time-warp map deforming clip content against timeline time.
Non-arrangement clip playback (scenes, launcher grids).
A gap between clips authored as a first-class item rather than absence.
One tempo governing the whole document.
Tempo changing over the document at more than one point.
One time signature governing the whole document.
Time signature changing over the document at more than one point.
A named point or range on the timeline.
The wall-clock timecode the document's zero position represents.
Where a media asset came from: source timecode, reel or tape name, original locator.
Static per-track gain.
Static per-track pan position.
Track routing to busses and auxiliary sends.
An automation lane targeting a device parameter.
An automation lane targeting a track's gain.
An automation lane targeting a track's pan.
A device occupying a slot in a track's chain, by identity.
A device's type and saved parameter state.
An effect that remaps time rather than processing content.
An alternate recording lane holding takes alongside the arrangement.
A composite assembled by selecting segments across takes.
A sealed offline render standing in for a track's live output.
Media identity derived from a content hash of the actual bytes.
Media bytes carried inside the document package.
Media referenced by locator, stored outside the document.
More than one sequence in the document.
A clip whose content is another sequence.
Typed extension clip content serialized through the schema registry.
Uninterpreted clip content carried in a validated envelope.
Positions at a rate that does not convert exactly to the document's rate.
A sequence-owned lane of chord and scale statements that other items read while compiling.
A sequence-owned groove: a swing setting and a repeating table of per-step timing and accent that other items read while compiling.
Per-note playback modifiers: probability, pass condition, and ratchet.
